clue.text: Leading doctor in Faroe Islands on holiday

parts.note: FO is the international country code for the Faroe Islands

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a holiday is a rest from work
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A senior doctor is spotted vacationing in the Faroe Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the islands' country code tops the answer and the doctor sits inside the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost and leading are synonyms meaning first in rank or position.

clue.text: Reminder for daughter

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A note left to jog a daughter's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A prod is a nudge or prompt, a reminder to get something done.

clue.text: Dropout's fruit tart

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: Someone who quit school or society enjoys a fruit tart.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippie is the classic dropout from conventional society of the 1960s counterculture.

clue.text: Male animal is last wandering big cat

indicators.note: letters that wander stray from their places and end up rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: The male animal trails behind while a big cat roams.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated adult male horse.

clue.text: Orleans regularly gets accolade for modernisation

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
an ovation is a burst of applause, an accolade

explanation.surface: The French city of Orleans is routinely praised for updating itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Renovation is restoring and updating a building, bringing it up to date.

clue.text: Last wife to back copy

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the last of Henry VIII's six wives

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A final wife decides to go back to imitating someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last wife' is the historical clue: Henry VIII's sixth and final queen, who outlived him.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or imitate mechanically, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: Attendant combining heart, they say, with rank

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: the core of something is its heart
a tier is a rank or level

explanation.surface: A servant manages to be both warm-hearted and high-ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech COUR at the start of the word sounds just like core.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is someone in attendance at a royal court.

clue.text: Least refined Conservative lost, becoming most abusive

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: crudest means least refined
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: The coarsest Tory loses his seat and turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudest is the superlative of rude, meaning most insulting or offensive.

clue.text: Worthless fellow taken back, getting time inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece is put within another
taken back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: got means taken
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A useless man is arrested and does time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Toerag is British slang for a contemptible person; the surface's prison picture makes 'time' look like a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is a British slang insult for a despicable or worthless person.

clue.text: Late award finally given to executed leader

indicators.note: someone executed by beheading loses the head, so the first letter goes
finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A posthumous honour is presented to a leader who was put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: An executed head literally loses its head, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the sense of deceased, as in 'the late king', means dead.

clue.text: It provides a range of footnotes

definitions.text: It provides a range of footnotes

parts.note: surface reading: a set of annotations at the bottom of a page
setter's reading: musical notes played with the feet, as on an organ

explanation.walkthrough: Footnotes sound like printed references, but they are notes sounded by feet on an organ's keyboard of pedals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalboard is the keyboard of pedals an organist plays with the feet, giving a range of bass notes.

clue.text: Nerve vessel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: courage, in British slang
second meaning: a container for liquids

explanation.walkthrough: Nerve vessel reads as anatomy; in British slang 'bottle' means courage, as in 'to lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for courage and also a narrow-necked container for drinks.

clue.text: Red and earthy like Chinese army

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the baked clay of the Xi'an warrior figures

explanation.walkthrough: The famous army of life-size soldiers buried near Xi'an in China is made of fired clay, hence earthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed fired clay and also the brownish-red colour of that material.

clue.text: Cut out six-footers' sporting gear

parts.note: to skip something is to cut it out or omit it
ants, like all insects, have six feet

explanation.surface: Tall people should leave out athletic clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footers suggests tall people, but here it means creatures with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are trousers worn for skiing, a piece of sports clothing.

clue.text: Upset about Mary's heart rate

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel, an upset

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters count

parts.note: the two central letters of the name

explanation.surface: A row has left Mary's pulse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a fixed rate or charge, such as a price list or import duty.

clue.text: Explanation of poor heating? It's gas

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words, a fire that is damp would heat badly
second meaning: the explosive methane found in coal mines

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into FIRE DAMP and it explains a cold room; as one word it is the miners' dreaded gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane that collects in coal mines and can explode.

clue.text: Ornament involves frantic searching without gas

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters are jumbled
without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Decorating involves a desperate hunt, with no gas to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G, A, S from SEARCHING to leave ERCHIN, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich is to adorn or embellish, making something richer in appearance.

clue.text: Stolen silverware getting warmer in kitchen

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
plate is silver or gold tableware

explanation.surface: Pilfered silver cutlery heats up in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotplate is a flat heated surface on a cooker for warming or cooking food.

clue.text: Go wrong hitting net when making return in sport

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: A player errs by hitting the net while returning serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a tennis match, so the sport is hiding in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played across a net.

clue.text: Give way in dreadful European conflict

indicators.note: in means placed within the other piece

parts.note: dire means dreadful
to sag is to sink or give way
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone concedes defeat in a terrible European war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conflict' is a verb here, matching DISAGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to conflict, to differ in opinion or fail to correspond.

clue.text: Set face up under current

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places one part below the other

parts.note: in means current or fashionable

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: Something is laid face up beneath a flowing stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid describes material set into a surface as decoration, such as wood or stone set flush.

clue.text: Native given a "thank you" for music

parts.note: a son of a place is a native of it, as in 'a son of Yorkshire'
taken as written
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A local is thanked for the tune he played.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a classical composition for one or two instruments, a piece of music.

clue.text: Phrase rewritten by angel

indicators.note: something rewritten is set down again in a new form, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angel revises a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels in Christian tradition.

clue.text: What he gives is soon back in circulation

definitions.text: What he gives is soon back in circulation

parts.words: What he gives is soon back in circulation
parts.note: surface reading: money or goods handed out soon return to general use
setter's reading: the bodily fluid he gives is replaced and flowing round the body again

explanation.walkthrough: Circulation suggests money or gossip, but it is the circulation of the bloodstream, which quickly makes good what was taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives blood finds the body replaces it within weeks.

clue.text: Much used water supplier to give notice, we're told

parts.note: a well supplies water

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the sound matters

parts.note: to warn is to give notice

explanation.surface: A busy water source is about to announce something.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation, without a sounded R, warn and worn sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-worn means showing signs of heavy use, or overused like a cliché.

clue.text: See 24 across
Police department returns with corporation ruling

indicators.note: something that returns goes back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
corporation is old jokey slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Detectives come back with a decision from the town council.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation looks like a business or council, but it is a humorous old word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictum is an authoritative pronouncement, a formal ruling.

clue.text: Corrupted tapes are put on one side

indicators.note: corrupted data is scrambled, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Damaged tapes get set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to set apart, to put something to one side away from the rest.
